events.summary: Parliament debated the second reading of the Central Bank of Samoa Amendment Bill 2026, which would stop the Governor chairing the bank's board, replacing her with an independent non-executive director, and require the bank's Executive Committee to give the Minister of Finance quarterly reports on policy and send the Minister the draft annual budget for comment within 14 working days. Prime Minister Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao Schmidt said the two roles should be separated and that the central bank belongs to the government. Opposition leader Tuilaepa Sailele Malielegaoi said the government had not accepted the IMF's advice; the report gives no passage or assent date, so the bill was not yet law when it was published on 19 August 2026.

events.summary: The Bank of Namibia announced on 19 November 2025 that Governor Johannes !Gawaxab would leave on 31 December 2025, a year before his term was due to expire, and gave no specific reason. No successor was named at the time. The report records no pressure from the government.

events.quote: will leave his position at the end of 2025, one year before his term is due to expire

searched_none.note: Read Jornal da Republica Serie I No 32 of 12 August 2026 (two passes, including the final and repealing provisions of Lei n.o 10/2026, the new general law on the financial system and banking activity): it does not amend Lei n.o 5/2011, the BCTL Organic Law, and gives the Minister or Government no power over the bank; art. 282 gives the BCTL its own regulatory power and art. 281 leaves appeals to the organic law. Read Serie I No 44 of 2011 (does not contain Lei n.o 5/2011). Read the Petroleum Fund quarterly report for 2024 Q4 (La'o Hamutuk copy): no change in who manages the Fund, no government direction to the BCTL, no amendment to the Petroleum Fund Law since 28 September 2011, and no change of governor; the Ministry of Finance and the bank work under a Management Agreement signed 25 June 2009. The only governor change found is Abrao de Vasconcelos succeeded by Helder Lopes in September 2023, which Central Banking reports as a succession with no statement that the term ended early. No instance found.

Searched for the Bank of Eritrea Proclamation No. 93/1997 text in FAOLEX, Ecolex, InforMEA and UNEP LEAP (they carry Eritrean land, fisheries and standards proclamations but no banking proclamation), and for any named Bank of Eritrea governor and how each term ended, including Kibreab Weldemariam. The Central Banking profile page for the Bank of Eritrea is behind a subscription wall and lists no governors. No proclamation text and no instance found.

Found the enacted law published in Official Gazette 16/25 on the National Bank's own site, in both Macedonian (Zakon-za-Narodnata-banka-16-25.pdf) and an English consolidated version (Law_on_the_National_bank-unoficial-version_16-25.pdf), but www.nbrm.mk returns 403 to automated requests, so the article text and the gazette date could not be read. Needs a hand check; both URLs are in leads_not_opened.

No instance of the Minister of Finance exercising the power of direction over the Bank of Namibia was found. Searched the Government Gazette archive (gazettes.africa), the Legal Assistance Centre law collection, NamibLII, the Bank of Namibia document library and Namibian press; the only ministerial-style determinations found are issued by the Bank or its Deputy Governor under the Banking Institutions Act, 1998, not by the Minister. Separately, the Namibia Economic Freedom Fighters' deputy leader Kalimbo Iipumbu asked the President to dismiss Governor !Gawaxab within seven days after a N$1 million Competition Commission fine over his own private shareholdings; the Namibian's page carries no publication date, so it is not filed.
